title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Kansas is moving from six digit license plate numbers to seven digit numbers because the state duplicates combinations. Matthew and Leah Spurlock own a minivan with a KU Alumni plate numbered 7007. A stolen GMC pickup had a temporary Kansas tag with the same number. Flock cameras alerted police, and the Spurlocks were pulled over in Colwich, Kansas. Police found the wrong plate type had been entered. Later, another Flock alert led Catoosa, Oklahoma, police to stop them at the Hard Rock Casino, where officers drew guns and handcuffed Matthew.

Police Capt. Casey Slaughter said Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not plate backgrounds, so alerts alone are not enough to stop a car. If a stolen tag is confirmed, officers have little choice. Kansas has more than 100 plate designs, about half specialty plates. Wichita police have discussed training Flock's AI to recognize plate backgrounds. The new seven digit, non duplicated numbers are the best solution. The Spurlocks' stolen entry has expired, so they are no longer worried and want to keep their 14 year old plate.
